messages.content: The world reforms. Briar's hands fumble around with the wooden instrument, producing some form of noise. She's young, very young, and has only just begun taking lessons from her brother. While not technically proficient, the song is still soulful.
"Why can't I play like you?" She pouts

Kit stifles a laugh. "Come on, sis, it's not a skill you learn overnight. It's taken me years to get to where I am. Believe it or not, I wasn't exactly a prodigy either. People would cover their ears and run when I'd pick up my tool of the trade."
"I don't believe you! you are the best at everything"

"Hah! Maybe I should go into marketing, or politics. Clearly I have a talent for overselling. I might have made up the running, but there really was a learning curve. I just didn't pout about." He gives her a playfully smug look.
"I'm trying!" with a scoff she starts playing once more
Her performance does not drastically improve in quality, but Kit continues to listen with a smile.
As she is done with the song she bows "That was better right? Right?"

He nods. "I'd say you're starting to get it. Still, we should work on some exercises to get your fundamentals down. Why don't we try-" As he speaks, footsteps come into earshot. "Ah. Tomorrow, then."

Briar's father opens the door. "Bedtime, kids."
She looks a little sad but nods "Fine, good night"
He doesn't look at her, just at Kit. "...You're teaching her the violin? I see. I was wondering why it sounded like that."
"Yes! I'm slowly getting better at it" she inserts herself in the conversation with excitement
"Slowly, huh?" He doesn't seem disappointed, just unimpressed. "...I guess we couldn't hope for more. You're not your brother." He leaves them to get ready for bed.
"I know..." she sighs with a weak smile.
"Goodnight Theo, I will do better tomorrow" she slowly walks away towards her room
"Th-that's not..." His words trail off, and he clicks his tongue as she walks away.

Briar closes the door behind her. She places the violin carefully on her table as she gets on her bed. As the silence sets in so do the feelings she had slowly learned to ignore during her short life. 

"I don't understand what I did so wrong... Do you know why father doesn't play with me? Or spend time with me? Or... talk to me?" she whispered grabbing a bunny plushie Theo had gifted her and speaking to it.
The bunny has no idea. There are zero thoughts in its head, and frankly, it would be concerning if there were any. What Briar hopes to accomplish with this is a mystery that may never be solved.
She hugs it as she gets underneath her blanket "I have you Beatrice and my brother... That's all I need"
There's a knock on her bedroom door.
She gets off her bed and slowly approaches her door, opening it just a crack.
Her mother is standing just past the door. "Oh, you're awake. Can I come in?"
She nods slowly, opening the door fully for her
She enters the room, taking a seat on the bed, and signaling for Briar to join her.
Briar closes the door and quickly goes to sit beside her. She a bit scared to talk herself waiting for her mother to have the first word.
Her mother stares ahead at the wall of the room. "I heard from your father. About you playing the violin."
"yes, Kit is teaching me"
"It's good to have hobbies." There's an uncomfortable pause. "When was the last time I read you a bedtime story? I can't recall."
Her eyes light up and a big smile appears in her face "Mom, are you going to read me one?"
She pulls a small book from her pocket. "I thought it would be pertinent."
Briar quickly gets under her blanket

"There once was a hill. Upon the hill sat a house. Within the house sat a woman. On the woman's lap sat a cat. Muddled and befuddled, the cat had lost its way. A shabby, tabby alley cat, happened upon her house."
Briar listened, the smile in her face widening

"She brushed and brushed the scruffy fur into a fluffy coat, and sent the cat upon its way. The woman felt good, having helped because she could. The next day, another cat appeared at her door. It twitched its whiskers and presented its paw, stuck with a splinter. Day after day, cats came, not to stay, but for help from the woman in the house on the hill. And the woman felt good, having helped so many because she could."
"She is making so many cat friends" Briar giggled

"One day, a very sick cat came upon the woman in the house on the hill. The woman wanted to help, but the cat continued to yelp. She tried all that she knew, old medicines and new. But the cat just cried and cried, no matter what she tried. She was at her wit's end. How could she help her feline friend?"
Little Briar's expression changes to one of worry

"There was a knock on her door, from a visitor she had not met before. The stranger felt wrong, it gave her a feeling of danger, but the words the stranger offered only made her feel heard. A solution to her troubles, a miracle potion filled with bubbles. With this, the stranger explained, under this roof a cat will remain."
"That's scary... But Mr. Cat won't make it"

"Despite her worry, she took the potion in a hurry. She rushed and rushed to the cat's side, and from the bottle's neck, the potion did gush. She opened the cat's mouth with her hand, and upon it did a splash of liquid land. The cat did not stir, it did not growl or purr. The cat was already gone, the potion had helped none.

"Confused, the woman felt a sensation where the potion had landed, upon her hand did grow a patch of fur. It spread and spread, from her hand to her head. Her hands changed to paws, a wet nose formed above her jaw. The potion was not for the cat as a cure, but as a transformation for her. Then, there was one cat, and it remained within the house, upon the hill. And it was sad, because it could not help anymore."
"That's so sad..." she grabbed her plushie hugging it close to her chest
She places the book back in her pocket. "Who do you think the stranger was?"
"A very mean person"

"I believe this story was inspired by tales of the Reaper, made appropriate for a younger audience. But yes, they certainly played a cruel trick. That is not what the story is about, though. The moral comes from the woman, and why she was tricked."
"She just wanted to help the kitty... What's wrong with that?"

"There's nothing wrong with doing what you can, but she let her ambition cloud her judgement. Before that, she helped the cats that should could. Simple tasks, like brushing their fur and removing their splinters. She should have known she could not have helped the sick cat. When people set their goals too high, trying to achieve dreams that are impossible for them, that's when they walk straight into danger. Maybe a doctor could have helped that cat, but she could never have, so she shouldn't have tried."
"There is nothing wrong with trying!" She sat up, her expression serious "The kitty had someone care about him, I'm sure that meant so much to him. She only needed to ask for help"
She stands up. "You'll understand when you're older. Go to sleep now." She leaves the room, shutting the door behind her.
"How can I sleep after something so sad...?" She laid back down. She didn't want to be alone but she shouldn't bother Kit at this time.

...She was alone, of course. Kit didn't come knocking on her door to comfort her, or anything. But... Well, this isn't a memory, is it? This is just a dream. Beatrice wraps her arms around Briar, and stays with her all night. Eventually, Briar peacefully falls asleep in her soft embrace.
**End Chapter 10.3**

The world reforms. A young Calamari sits with her friend Mike Acilis, commonly known as Ace, in the center of a park. It's a nice day. Flowers are in bloom, and bird songs fill the air. Ace stares at the sky, watching the clouds pass by.
I fall backwards onto the grass. "Perfect."
"...Yeah. Kinda wish everyday could be like this."
I laugh. "Every day kind of has been like this for a while, don't you think? When was the last time somebody stopped you from going to the park?"
"All the time. My mom and dad are always fussing about studying, and praying, and boring stuff like that. You got lucky, Mari. Religious parents are the worst."
I push myself up onto my elbow to look at him. "What, you can't sneak away for a couple minutes? Not even at night?"
"Well, I guess it wouldn't be the day anymore, then. Ha! Never mind, you win."
I drop back down, splaying out even further than before.
"Still, I'm glad we're getting to do this. It's really pretty..."
"Yeah..." He lays down next to Mari, and proceeds to point towards a particular cloud. "What do you think that one looks like? Isn't it kinda strange?"
"Hm... nah, I think it's pretty normal, actually. Kind of looks like..." I think about it for a few seconds. "A violin?"
"The little pointy bit at the top... and there's that other cloud next to it too, like it's the bow!"
I point between them. "See what I mean?"
"Mmm... I guess? Actually, yeah, I think I do see it. Just... took a second."
"Really? I dunno, I think it's pretty obvious."
"Glad you get it though, Cilly."
I smile up at the cloud.

Embarrassing behavior, really. Ace lowers his hand, folding them across his body. "At first, I thought... I mean, you're probably right about the violin thing, but... at first I thought it kinda looked like a tower."
"What would the other cloud even be, then? A really thin second tower?" I say jokingly.
I point at a third, nearby cloud. "Maybe that one is heading for them... uh oh."
"No, they're definitely a violin and bow. The shape just doesn't make any sense for a tower. Why would the bottom be thinner than the middle? What kind of a tower is that?"

"...Um, just asking, but... I don't think violins have a thinner bottom than middle? They always have that, like, eight shape? Like, the number eight? I don't know why, but... don't they all have that middle dip?"
"The number eight also gets really thin at the bottom. When the lines come together..."
"But violins have a taller bottom circle than top circle, so the middle is still a little stretched out in comparison to the lower edge."
"They're like people, basically. Y'know?"
"That makes sense... So, what's the third cloud? Like, is it, um, a hand? Going to play the violin, right?" He tries to offer a helpful suggestion.
"No, that one isn't related to the first two, I was just joking. It's a squid, see?" I outline all the tentacles with my finger.
"Oh! I just read a story about a squid! Well, I mean, it was a kraken, but... I think that's a type of squid? It has tentacles, at least."
"Yeah... probably."

"What happened to it in the story? Ooh, I bet it tried to wreck some massive boat... but then all the sailors on board banded together to fend it off. Type of thing that tends to happen to krakens, eh?"
"Well... actually, the sailors all got gobbled up when they tried. The kraken just kept breaking ships and stuff, it was a real menace! That's why it was so cool when the Hero showed up to slay it."
"Oh." I frown. "Well, I dunno. What made the hero so special, that she succeeded where all the sailors failed?"
"It sounds like this squid was pretty gnarly."

"Well... I guess because the Hero had been learning to fight since birth? I mean, they needed to rescue the Prince, you know? But the sailors were just... sailors. They can sail ships really well, but that's about it."
"Sailing makes you strong!" I raise my right arm to comically flex it. "Throwing the anchor aweigh! Pulling the ropes into the hole! Tossing those barrels around! It's tough work, man!"
"I get what you mean, though. Sounds like none of them would have thought to bring a sword on their voyage."
"I guess sometimes you need a specific type of person to get the job done. Still feels a bit wrong to me, though."
"I dunno."
"This stuff is complicated. Maybe you should put down the books for a bit and get some real work done. Nerd." I poke his shoulder.

"But I am working! Or, um, you know, I'm working up to working. I don't just read Panthium books, I read all kinds. The more you know, the more fields you can work in! I mean, I guess... not all jobs. Some you can just be strong, like sailing..."
"Wait, the squid story was part of your religious stuff? So it really happened?"
"Yeah. I know it's a bit far-fetched, but... there really are some great people out there, and who knows what kinda monsters are out at the edge of the ocean?"
"Why would they be at the edge, doofus? If you're a big squid, are you gonna stay in the spot where you fall off a cliff as soon as you go to sleep, or in the normal zone?"
"Everything interesting definitely sticks right around the middle. That's why we're here."
"Oh, uh, yeah, well... I don't think we've explored all of the middle of the ocean either? So... it could still happen."
"Imagine how many fish they have to eat each day to stay alive. Hehe."
"You know, you kind of remind me of a fish, Cilly. You would be a good trout, I bet."
"Or maybe a salmon..."
"Why a salmon? I'm not really sure I get it..."
"Well, you know, they're all pale and floppy! Just like you, ya weirdo."
"And they always end up right back at home. No matter how hard they try to get away, they wind up back where they started. Just like you were saying, right?"

"Is that what I was saying? Well... I mean, I guess in that case, I'll just have to wait for a Hero to save me from the kraken. I don't really wanna get eaten, you know? And if the sailors can't do it, what chance does a salmon have?"

"I'm sure the salmon have their own hero. What kind of human would go beat up a giant squid just to save a fish, right? You'll have to find a salmon knight... or maybe he'll be a trout, actually. I bet all the fish get along. The kraken eats all of them, so it makes more sense that way."
I ponder the aquatic lore.
"Do you know which fish are the biggest, Cilly?"
"A trout might be too small, is what I'm thinking..."
"Well, I'm not sure that really matters... I don't think the Hero was the biggest human around, either. It's, um, you know, about just being the best! Not the biggest, or anything."
"People are way bigger than fish." I say this like he's completely stupid, which he is.
"Oh." He pauses to think. "Well, maybe it'll be another squid? We already know they're pretty big." He points to the clouds again. "The Squid Hero, come to save the Prince trapped in the tower."

"How did the prince get trapped inside a violin? Is he some sort of idiot?!" I push myself over into Ace's line of sight to make a comically baffled face at him, then jab him in the stomach a few times.

"Ow! Hey!" He protests with a wide grin, lightly pushing her away. How interesting that the two of them can come to such wildly different conclusions from the same simple shapes. The contents of the outline changed completely, just from who it is filling the clouds.
**End Chapter 10.3**

Alonsa stands in the center hall of the church, welcoming a woman from the town. She appears to be searching for something, or someone. She wears a calm, soft smile as she glances around, but something about her body language puts Alonsa on edge.
“Welcome!” Alonsa raises her arms in greeting.

"Yes. I am welcomed, welcomed indeed." She fixes her gaze on Alonsa. "The boy. I know he visits here. I am concerned, ever so concerned for him. We have not been able to locate him, my family and I. You would not know anything, would you?"

It's true, he has visited the church often since that burial, but it's been several days since he was last seen.
“I’m sorry, I haven’t seen him.”
"That's too bad, and quite so sad. Do let me know if that changes, won't you? I am afraid he has left us in a rather tough spot. Everyone must contribute their fair share, wouldn't you agree?"
“Of course.”
“He’s yours, after all.”
She nods. After a moment, she exits the church.
Alonsa sighs.

The Father's voice resounds from the next room. He appears to have been close enough to overhear the conversation. "So, his family is unaware of his whereabouts?" He enters the room. His whole body, vertically aligned, is allowed through the doorway at more or less the same moment. "I had made the presumption that they had been keeping him busy... If he is neither here, nor there... What could have occurred?"
"Perhaps he is here."
"Hiding, somewhere in the church."

"..." He places a hand to his chin, considering it. "That may be the most worrying outcome. He is certainly not vicinity of these entrance halls. If he went further... Could he retrace his steps? They are much too labyrinthine, for one unfamiliar..."
"We should search, then,'
"Just in case. Before it's too late."

He nods. The two of them begin their search, weaving through the sandstone corridors. The halls are dark, but the Father takes a torch to illuminate their path. Their steps echo down the halls, and so on. Eventually, something peculiar comes into sight. The boy, now grown into a teenager, appears to be trapped beneath something. His leg is pinned by a cave-in, revealing the bare stone behind the carved walls.

"Ah. My child. What a relief it is to find you, at last. We were all worried, quite so." The Father does not appear to notice the danger the boy is in. His eyesight has been waning in recent years.
She rushes over to him. "What happened!?"
"...Isn't it obvious? Wrong place, wrong time, I guess. Freak accident... just my luck." The boy seems resigned to his lot in in life.
"Poor child..."
She attempts to move the stones.
...Wouldn't that be nice? They're heavy, and massive. It's hard to get a grip, and harder to muster the strength needed. The boy just seems confused. "...What are you doing?"
She tries anyway. "You shouldn't have come here alone. It's dangerous!"
"Well, duh. I know it's dangerous. That keeps most people back, at least. It was just... somewhere I can hide, 'til this all blows over. Coming with someone else would defeat the point."
"Till what blows over? How long have you been coming here?" She does her best not to sound accusatory
"Just... Uuuu... You know! I was just playing their stupid game. I may have rigged it a little, but I swindled them fair and square! That's part of the fun! And now they're... they want me to pay!"
"Child... you know better..."

"Better according to who? It's just... exhilarating. You wouldn't get it... You Panthium folks are a part of the community. You're a pillar! But me... Just- just for a moment, people stop looking at me like..." He doesn't seem able to find the words to finish that sentence.
“You can’t find a place for yourself hiding in the tunnels, child.”
“And especially not with a rock on your leg.”
“Father, what shall we do?”

The Father... Yes, he hasn't spoken in a while, has he? Alonsa just threw things off track... It's difficult to keep events playing out the same. What was it he said here? How about this.

"The cave-in presents a difficulty, certainly. We may need to return with additional hands. As for our Child's predicament on the surface... I believe I may have a solution."
"Yes?"

"...My Child, how much do you owe these men?"

The boy seems almost offended by the idea of repayment. "Th-that's not! It's not about the money, it's the pride! It's like, their fucking ego! These guys are gonna fucking kill me, Father! I can't go out there!"

The Father grabs hold of a golden necklace he always keeps on his personage. It's a cross, a vital symbol of Panthium. "Would this be enough to satisfy these men?"
“Father, are you certain…?”

He nods. "It is merely a fancy trinket. The form carries meaning, not the material. If I am wrong, I am sure it will find its own way back here, do you not think? All tends to find itself linked to its home."
“That’s true…” she says, but she still looks nervous.

The boy looks equally as nervous. "Well, uh... thanks, but... you really don't have to do that for me. I'm just being a pussy, honestly. Throw me to the wolves, it'll be... fine."

The Father shakes his head. "Those words are mere platitudes. You know it is impossible that could ever convince me. For your pain is my own. I weep learning that you still face such adversity, as much as you seem unable to tear yourself away from activities inviting of it."
“The father is offering you another chance, child.”

"I know, I know. It's just..." The boy seems to anguish over the decision. As he does, the Father releases his grip on the golden cross.

"It is your decision, my Child. Now then, #$%@&, we should retrieve help. I am sure our Child has already remained in these tunnels for far too long. To delay another moment would be unwise."
“Alright. Would it be wise for us both to go? I feel one of us should stay while the other gets help.”

"Ah, yes. In that case, I will remain with- NO!" His eyes lock onto something in front of him. He throws out a hand, reaching to stop the boy, but he's too late.

"Just... gotta... damn!" The boy snaps something in his leg. The wet crunch is painful even to hear. With its position twisted, he's able to pull it out from beneath the rubble.
She looks on in complete horror, and puts her hands in front of her mouth

The Father is furious. He looks ready to burst a blood vessel. "YOU... FOOLISH... Auughh... My child, you merely needed to wait. Assistance would have arrived shortly. This needless violence! These... destructive instincts! Your pain is not something so trivial, to be thrown around on whims!"

The boy doesn't meet his eyes, staring at the floor instead. "What's the problem? Yeah, it hurts like a bitch, but it worked... You guys don't gotta do everything for me."
“Do you realize what you’ve done to yourself? You might not walk ever again!”
“You cannot… you must not abuse your body in this way. You will get yourself killed…”
The wording is stern, but she says it caringly

"...It's fine. No one would've come and helped. Just you guys. I-I can do it myself. It's like... you know, when a wolf gnaws off its own leg? 'Cause it's like, caught in a trap. It has to. I had to do this. It's just... this is my nature. I feel alive when I do this." It's hard to see beneath his pained expression, but a slight smile rises to his face.
“Poor child…”
“This cannot… this cannot end well for you. You’re going to die of this, someday.”
“I can’t… the church can’t accept you simply throwing your life away.”

The Father nods, calming himself. "I am inclined to agree. We cannot simply stand by and watch. As for now, you will be treated above ground. I shall bring you there. There is no need for you to strain yourself, it shall only bring further harm to-"

"Hey, Father? What's... up with those holes?" The boy interrupts him, pointing to something unveiled by the cave-in. Behind the carved sandstone, something was lurking. Four holes. Alonsa knows the ones.
((End session))
Alonsa moves to help him to his feet.
“Those… You shouldn’t worry yourself with those.”

"Huh? Why not? I mean, they kinda look like people. Are they bad guys, or something?" The boy is successfully helped to his feet.

"I..." The Father considers the shapes. "I have no idea who they are. No one I recognize."
She doesn’t respond to what the child says, instead looking onto the hole. Of course, she knows about the holes. One of them is for her. For Alonsa. She’s Alonsa, isn’t she?

But, at the same time, she doesn’t know about them. She’s not supposed to. Alonsa won’t walk through these halls for many many more years. The person who walks through these halls and sees the holes is… her? But she’s here, now.
She puts her hand to her head. Her head pounds and aches.
She looks at the holes, and sees, for the first time, something she won’t see for the first time until many years from now, long after she’s dead.

As Alonsa loses her grip on herself, the world seems to follow suit. The environment shifts to another scene. Alonsa and The Father are carrying crates to the town square. Each is filled with supplies recently delivered from another Panthium church. Paradise's harvests have hit an all-time low, leading to famine and a lack of incoming funds from trade, so it was decided that intervention by the church was required.
Alonsa ungrips her head, not even sure what she was concerned about. The headache remains.
She grips the crate with both hands, and holds onto it tightly

As they reach the town square, the boy comes into view, seated on the fountain. Upon seeing them, he reaches for his cane, and stands with some difficulty. His leg has healed, some, but it will never be the same. With a wave, he shouts to them. "Hey! What's with all the boxes?"
“We’ve come to help with the famine.”
“Inside are dried rations.”
The Father nods. "Indeed. Eventually, this town will be rewarded for its worship, and these hardships shall end. Until that time, it is our responsibility to assist one another."
“The act of believing in a better future, that is the very core of faith itself.”

"A better future, huh? Guess that'd be nice... Maybe I just live in the moment too much."

As the boy speaks, The Father places his crate near the base of the fountain.
Alonsa places hers down as well
As Alonsa places her crate, a glint of metal by the fountain seems to catch her eye. There appears to be a key embedded into the brickwork of the fountain.
She looks down at it, then tries to fish it out.

The key retrieval is achieved without a hitch. Next to her, The Father stares at the boy's leg. There's a sadness in his eyes, regrets and painful memories, but there's something else, too.

"My child, if it is alright... I have made a recent discovery. I believe it may be of some help to you."
Alonsa listens, but doesn’t say anything.

"Huh? I mean, I'm listening." The boy doesn't seem to know what to expect.

"Since my arrival in this town, I have perused the texts contained within its church. Many of them are copies, frequent in any location with Panthium followers. Some, though... some are unique to this town. Detailing its history. Its practices, lost to time. There is something I wish to try." The Father takes a moment to collect his thoughts. "My child, how would you like to be able to walk perfectly once again? As if nothing had even happened?"
**End Chapter 100**
Atie can't speak.

Atie's eyes open. There's enough light to take in her surroundings. Those sandstone tunnels. She's still in them. It's not the same hall in which she tripped. It's much more familiar than that. She's been here before. In a dream. In a nightmare. This isn't a dream. She can feel it. For once in her life, she's truly awake. Her body is whole, and her mind is solid.

In front of her is a hole. It should be the shape of her body, but isn't. She knows that, but doesn't know why. It's filled with something, but it's not her. There's three other human-shaped holes, all filled with something. Down one end of the hall is a cave-in, blocking the path out. Down the other is an open door, adorned with four keyholes and four matching keys. There's a rythmic beating coming from past the door.

Atie looks for anyone. She wasn't alone before. She suspects the others would be beyond the cave-in, but they shouldn't have been split. Something is past that door, but she can't bring herself there. She carefully gets closer to the cave-in, and listens for any other sound.
Either there is nothing moving beyond the cave-in, or the wall of rocks is simply too thick to hear through. It sounds like something may be happening above her, but it is indistinct.
She leans on a wall, stressed, still away from the door. She keeps listening, trying to understand what could be happening.

...It's quiet, but there does seem to be something else. It's difficult to hear underneath the repeated noises originating from the door. It sounds closer, but fading quickly. It sounds like... breathing. There's something breathing nearby.
[How can I hear this breathing from here?]
The breathing seems to be coming from the hole. Whatever is filling this hole, in which Atie herself should be able to fit, is alive. It's breathing. For now.
[What is this?]

It's your replacement. What do you think?

Flesh-colored, twisted and rearranged to fit the shape. Several pieces of a human form are recognizable within the living mass. Organs misplaced and misshapen. A heart and lungs, muscle and sinew, bones melted and cooled into place. It's the shape of a human. The shape that should be yours. Now, it will suffer in your place. Congratulations, Atie Alcule. She saved you.
[No... No... That doesn't make sense... What... is this?]

She could tell you. Not like this, of course, but she'd be able to explain when free. It's up to you. Do you value the answers? Do you want to learn how you got here? Or will you trust her? Will you let her suffer in your place? Is this where your story will end? You can remain here until your dying day. No one will judge you, Atie Alcule.
[I don't know. I don't know about any answers. What about me? Why do I have to be replaced? What's wrong with just going forward with life? What did I do to deserve this mess?]

That should be obvious. You did nothing. Nothing at all. You had every chance to stop this. You had every chance to make a decision. Instead, you stood by idly. You learned, and you observed. You anchored yourself to the world. So, will anything really change with someone else at the helm?

There's something else in the hole. In the living mass of flesh. As if stuck onto it as an afterthought, something is tangled within the organic matter. It's your wristwatch. It seems to have stopped. How long could it have possibly been?
[Is that my watch? Is it really the same one? That's not the same as me either. This is all wrong.]

No, this is right. This is how it is. You've been given more than enough. Rot down here, live a long lonely life, or get in the hole and accept your role. The only one this matters to is you, so you get to decide.
Atie becomes more panicked and decides to investigate the door.

The door is thick and sturdy, carved of sandstone with care. The rhythmic palpitations are audible behind it. The sounds of life. Larger than any sound Atie has ever heard. There is something inhuman beyond that door. Yet, something familiar.
Atie exits through the door regardless. It's the only option left.

The beating gets louder, and louder, as she walks. The halls are filled with... webs, or perhaps roots? They burst from the walls, floor, and ceiling, wrapping around one another like spider silk. As she walks, they become more frequent, and difficult to avoid. The threads become ropes, and their material becomes clear. The halls are covered in tendrils of flesh. Each one pulsates with ferocity. It's hard to look past them, but she can see the end of the hall. The solid sandstone wall. There's something there, something connected to these gnarled branches of flesh. She might be able to see it if she were to shove past them.
((End session))
Atie closes her eyes. She moves forward slowly with one of her arms extended, expecting but fearing the moment it comes into contact with these things.

As she pushes past them, a sensation creeps across her arms. Wet, soft, and alive. It's not quite rigid, but not quite malleable either, holding its shape but flexing to her touch like a contracted muscle. Eventually, as she walks, she stops feeling the strange surface against her skin.
[Am I... past that?]

Atie watches, disturbed.
"...It's not pleasant, is it?" A familiar voice rings into Atie's ear from behind.

She sees Penny, standing just ahead of tendrils Atie passed through. There was clearly no one here before, but somehow, now she sees Penny. Except... it's clearly not her. She has her clothes, her skin, her eyes and hair. But her shape... it's different. It's no longer hers.

"..." She moves towards Atie, and shoves her hand forward. Straight into Atie's chest. Penny's arm passes right through, like she isn't even there. "We... have a lot to talk about."

"I-I'm not even sure where to start. D-do you... have any questions?"

Atie is filled with dread. Penny has hardly made anything clearer, but it keeps getting scarier.
"No... No... Why don't you... understand me...? Stay away..."

Atie almost reflexively says "no", but before committing to it, she realizes she doesn't know what it is yet. It's something about her body... She looks closely at her arms and hands, and tries to find any way to see if her face is different.

Her skin tone is darker, and her hands aren't the shape she remembers. In her pocket, she's able to find a small mirror, perfect for this context.
